# Automatically Generated Firewall Rules

| Rule | Interface | Protocol | Source | Destination | Port | Purpose |
|------|-----------|----------|--------|-------------|------|---------|
| Block All IPv6 | Global | IPv6 | Any | Any | Any | Drops all IPv6 traffic since IPv6 is disabled. |
| Default Deny / State Violation | Global | Any | Any | Any | Any | Drops traffic that does not match an existing state or firewall rule. |
| Block Port 0 | Global | TCP/UDP | Any | Any | Port 0 | Blocks invalid TCP/UDP packets targeting port 0. |
| Block Port 0 | Global | TCP/UDP | Any | Any | Port 0 | Additional protection against invalid TCP/UDP traffic. |
| SSH Lockout Protection | Global | TCP | SSH Lockout Table | This Firewall | 22 | Prevents administrators from locking themselves out of SSH management. |
| HTTPS Lockout Protection | Global | TCP | SSH Lockout Table | This Firewall | 443 | Prevents administrators from locking themselves out of the web GUI. |
| VirusProt Overload Table | Global | Any | VirusProt Table | Any | Any | Automatically blocks IP addresses placed into the overload table. |
| DHCP Broadcast | VLAN 20 | UDP | Any | 255.255.255.255 | 67 | Allows DHCP Discover broadcasts from VLAN 20 clients. |
| DHCP Server Access | VLAN 20 | UDP | Any | This Firewall | 67 | Allows DHCP requests to reach the OPNsense DHCP server. |
| Firewall Self-Traffic | Global | Any | Firewall | Any | Any | Allows traffic generated by the firewall itself to leave the system. |
| Anti-Lockout (HTTP) | LAN | TCP | Any | This Firewall | 80 | Prevents accidental loss of HTTP management access from the LAN interface. |
| Anti-Lockout (HTTPS) | LAN | TCP | Any | This Firewall | 443 | Prevents accidental loss of HTTPS management access from the LAN interface. |

---

# Manual Firewall Rules

## Floating Rules 

| Rule | Interface | Source | Destination | Protocol | Purpose |
|------|-----------|--------|-------------|----------|---------|
| Web GUI Access | Floating | 192.168.50.10 | Any | IPv4 | Allows management workstation access to the homelab |


## Interface Rules

| Priority | Interface | Action | Protocol | Source | Destination | Port | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|--------|----------|--------|-------------|------|---------|
| 1 | LAN | Allow | IPv4 | LAN Network | Any | Any | Default outbound access for LAN devices. |
| 2 | VLAN 10 | Allow | IPv4 | VLAN10 Network | Any | Any | Allows backend infrastructure to access the Internet. |
| 3 | VLAN 20 | Allow | IPv4 | VLAN20 Network | Any | Any | Allows frontend client devices to access the Internet. |
| 4 | VLAN 20 | Allow | TCP/UDP | VLAN20 Network | Windows Server (192.168.10.30) | DNS (53) | Allows clients to resolve domain names through the Active Directory DNS server. |
| 5 | VLAN 20 | Allow | TCP/UDP | VLAN20 Network | Windows Server (192.168.10.30) | NTP (123) | Allows clients to synchronize time with the domain controller. |
| 6 | VLAN 20 | Allow | TCP/UDP | VLAN20 Network | Windows Server (192.168.10.30) | LDAP (389) | Allows Active Directory authentication and directory services. |
| 7 | VLAN 20 | Allow | TCP/UDP | VLAN20 Network | Windows Server (192.168.10.30) | SMB (445) | Allows clients to access Active Directory file services and domain resources. |
| 8 | VLAN 20 | Allow | TCP/UDP | VLAN20 Network | TrueNAS (192.168.10.20) | SMB (445) | Allows clients to access shared network storage on the NAS. |
| 9 | VLAN 20 | Block | IPv4 | VLAN20 Network | VLAN10 Network | Any | Prevents unrestricted access from the frontend VLAN to backend infrastructure while permitting only explicitly allowed services. |

# NAT Rules (Outbound Hybrid Mode)

| Interface | Source Network | Destination | Translation | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| WAN | VLAN10 Network (192.168.10.0/24) | Any | WAN Interface Address | Allows Backend VLAN devices to access the Internet |
| WAN | VLAN20 Network (192.168.20.0/24) | Any | WAN Interface Address | Allows Frontend VLAN devices to access the Internet |
